Maximum margin : when drawing a boundary between two classes, attempt to maximize the width of the boundary (SVM). The assumption is that distinct classes tend to be separated by wide boundaries.
Common inductive bias in ML:
Minimum description length : when forming a hypothesis, attempt to minimize the length of the description of the hypothesis. The assumption is that simpler hypotheses are more likely to be true.

tree.name: Inductive Bias
tree.content: Inductive bias comprises assumptions that guide a learning algorithm to prefer certain hypotheses over others, shaping model selection.

details.content: Inductive bias is the set of assumptions that influence hypothesis preference in machine learning.

tree.name: Maximum Conditional Independence
tree.content: Maximum conditional independence bias favors hypotheses where features are conditionally independent given the class, exemplified by Naive Bayes.

details.content: Maximum conditional independence is applied when the hypothesis can be cast in a Bayesian framework, trying to maximize conditional independence (Naive Bayes classifier).
Maximum conditional independence encourages the use of Naive Bayes classifier as it assumes feature independence given the class.

tree.name: Minimum Cross-Validation Error
tree.content: Minimum cross-validation error bias selects the hypothesis that achieves the lowest error estimate across validation folds.

details.content: When choosing among hypotheses, select the hypothesis with the lowest cross-validation error.
Minimum cross-validation error aims to reduce overfitting by evaluating model performance on held‑out data.

tree.name: Maximum Margin
tree.content: Maximum margin bias prefers decision boundaries that maximize the distance between classes, forming the basis of Support Vector Machines.

details.content: When drawing a boundary between two classes, attempt to maximize the width of the boundary (SVM).
Maximum margin assumes distinct classes tend to be separated by wide boundaries.

tree.name: Minimum Description Length
tree.content: Minimum description length bias favors simpler hypotheses with shorter descriptive length, assuming simplicity correlates with truth.

details.content: When forming a hypothesis, attempt to minimize the length of the description of the hypothesis.
The assumption is that simpler hypotheses are more likely to be true.

tree.name: Minimum Features
tree.content: Minimum features bias removes features unless strong evidence demonstrates their usefulness, simplifying the model.

details.content: Unless there is good evidence that a feature is useful, it should be deleted.
Minimum features bias encourages feature elimination to avoid unnecessary complexity.

tree.name: Nearest Neighbor
tree.content: Nearest neighbor bias assumes that instances close in feature space are likely to share the same class label.

details.content: Assume that most of the cases in a small neighborhood in feature space belong to the same class.
Nearest neighbor bias underlies k‑nearest neighbor classification methods.
